title: TS SDK: Stream Interop Conciliation Guide and Adapter
creator: Maya Kapoor
description: Deliver a small, well-tested TypeScript adapter and a short guidance doc that enables safe, ergonomic interoperation between AsyncIterator-based consumers and Web Streams-based producers (and vice-versa) in the TS SDK. The adapter should handle cancellation propagation, backpressure coordination, graceful resume for resumable streams, and provide easy examples for app authors.
background: There are many existing internal tickets addressing pieces of stream interop (async iterator vs ReadableStream) and streaming ergonomics. Customers and internal SDK users expect simple examples that 'just work' across Node/Deno/Browser. Previous approaches duplicated buffering logic or introduced surprising cancellation semantics. We need a single conciliatory primitive that is lightweight, clearly documented, and compatible with our streaming contracts (resume, abort, retry, and fallback patterns).
proposal: Implement a 'Conciliator' adapter that exposes two light-weight helper factories: 1) fromAsyncIteratorToReadableStream(asyncIterable, options) and 2) fromReadableStreamToAsyncIterator(readable, options). The adapter will: (a) maintain a single internal buffer with bounded capacity, (b) coordinate backpressure signals using the ReadableStream controller's desiredSize and a Promises-based pull loop for async iterators, (c) propagate AbortSignal/cancellation in both directions, and (d) emit optional 'resume tokens' for checkpointing resumable producers. The implementation will live in packages/sdk/stream-utils and be shipped in the next minor release of the TS SDK.
technical_design: Key implementation choices: - Bounded ring buffer with async waiters: avoids unbounded memory growth while keeping CPU overhead low. - Backpressure heuristics: default capacity 8 chunks; controller.desiredSize checks inform the iterator's pull pacing. - Cancellation semantics: when an AbortSignal is received, the adapter will call underlying cancel/return on the source if available and settle pending read promises with a DOMException('AbortError'). - Resume tokens: optional metadata object attached to certain chunk frames (string token) so the consumer can persist offsets. - Errors: adapter surface ensures source errors bubble to both consumer styles. - Node/Browser specifics: use global ReadableStream when present; fall back to web-streams-polyfill in Node < 18. - API ergonomics: keep the surface minimal, accept an options bag (capacity, attachResumeToken, onBackpressure callback).
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Introducing resume tokens couples the adapter to a minimal framing scheme. We expose tokens as optional and do not force framing; heavy users can opt-in. - A bounded internal buffer could introduce latency if capacity is too small; we will land with conservative default and expose tuning. - Polyfill dependencies for Node environments increase bundle size slightly; we'll lazily import polyfills only when needed.
acceptance_criteria: Conciliator functions export and type-check in TS SDK package
Round-trip test: async iterator -> ReadableStream -> async iterator preserves chunk order and abort semantics
Backpressure test: consumer slow-down prevents unbounded memory growth in producer-heavy scenario
Cancellation test: AbortSignal from either side triggers underlying source cancellation when available
Resume token opt-in example persists and restores stream position in an integration test
Documentation: one-page guide + three copy-paste examples (Node, Deno, Browser) in repo docs
test_plan: Unit tests for ring buffer edge cases (empty, full, concurrent pulls)
Integration test in CI: simulate high-throughput producer and slow consumer; assert memory stays bounded
Cross-runtime smoke: run example in Node 16(with polyfill), Node 18, Deno, and Chromium CI image
Fuzz test: random chunk sizes and intermittent AbortSignals to validate no hangs or leaks
Type tests: compile-time ensure exported generics preserve chunk typing
rollout_plan: MVP release in canary/tagged beta for internal SDK consumers (2 weeks)
Collect feedback from SDK integrators and Solutions Eng; iterate defaults if needed
Promote to stable in next minor if no regressions and acceptance criteria met
Add a short 'migration' FAQ for customers relying on older ad-hoc adapters
